clue.text: Obstinate resistance overcome by works on divinity?

indicators.note: on places one piece after another, so the divinity letters come first

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject once called divinity

indicators.note: overcome by means the resistance letter is surrounded and swamped by the works

parts.note: a works is a factory
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A stubborn opposition is defeated by theological writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works on divinity' reads as theological books, but works is FACTORY and divinity is RE, the school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes someone stubborn and unmanageable, a synonym of obstinate.

clue.text: Coming up, surface, speak, and vanish

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to pave is to surface a road
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A list of things a figure does, rising, surfacing, talking, then disappearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to disappear like vapour, so it can mean vanish.

clue.text: Cleared up leaves, say, on a slope

definitions.meaning: ... describes gathering fallen leaves with a rake
a ... stage or seat bank is inclined

explanation.surface: A gardener tidying leaves on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Raked means both gathered with a rake and set at an incline, as a theatre stage is.

clue.text: In bed, recommend borders of thyme — this could supply kitchen

indicators.note: In puts the recommend word inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
to urge is to recommend strongly

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Planting advice: thyme edging a bed will stock the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' and 'thyme' paint a herb garden, but bed is COT and borders of thyme gives TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette is a garden vegetable, the sort of produce a kitchen garden supplies to the cook.

clue.text: Return ticket to continental interior?

parts.note: a return ticket takes you out and then home again; the continental interior is Australia's remote bush

explanation.surface: A traveller buying a round trip into the middle of a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'return ticket' as a journey there and home again; the phrase for that names the Australian bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian bush interior bears the name made of the two words for going away and coming home.

clue.text: Envy finally gnaws at poet

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of envy

parts.note: something that gnaws at you eats away at you

explanation.surface: Jealousy eventually eats away at a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: W.B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Computer controls people lacking character

definitions.meaning: pointing devices moved by hand to steer a computer
timid people are called mousy, each one a mouse

explanation.surface: A complaint that those running the computers are spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are both computer pointing devices and, figuratively, timid people without spirit.

clue.text: Italian poet races between soldier and one Roman

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy
TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A poet from Italy watches a race between a soldier and a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the standard crossword abbreviation for the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti was the Italian poet who founded Futurism.

clue.text: Right to move into liquid assets before stock market does this?

indicators.note: the right letter moves into the middle of the assets word

parts.note: cash is the most liquid asset

explanation.surface: Advice to shift into cash just before the markets fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Markets are said to crash when share prices collapse suddenly.

clue.text: Stop arms manufacturer short, taking time out of business

parts.note: to ban something is to stop it

indicators.note: short means the maker's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Krupp was the German armaments firm

explanation.surface: Halting a weapons maker's supply and letting time pass puts a firm under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims KRUPP to KRUP; 'taking' just adds T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankrupt firm cannot pay its debts and so has gone out of business.

clue.text: A minor thoroughfare in France, say

parts.note: ... is a minor road in the British road system, below an A road

explanation.surface: A small country lane somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A roads are main roads, B roads are minor ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, and being in France is an example of that for a Briton.

clue.text: To bring back trophy, follow one who's most successful

indicators.note: bring back means the trophy word is turned round

parts.note: a pot is slang for a cup won as a trophy
to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Whoever brings the cup home follows the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A top dog is an idiom for the leading or dominant person.

clue.text: Bane, this, when drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests a confused state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A warning that this spirit is a curse once consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a notorious green spirit thought ruinous by drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe, the strong wormwood spirit, was blamed for ruin and madness, a bane when drunk.

clue.text: Carry on with period

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going for a while longer.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry on means to conduct, as in to wage a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage war or a campaign is to carry it on.

clue.text: Go on at length, writing, say, from exile

indicators.note: from means the writing letter is taken away from the exile word

parts.note: an expatriate lives in exile from his home country
writing is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: An exiled author writes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so writing gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at great length on a subject.

clue.text: Have some whisky and invite censure

parts.note: to take a drink is to have it
a tot is a small measure of spirits
to ask someone is to invite them

explanation.surface: Pouring a whisky and asking for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is the idiom for rebuking them, so it matches censure.

clue.text: Fluid I rated wet

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone judging a liquid as damp.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue doubles as a description: water that flows with the tide is fluid and wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidewater is water brought in by the tide, which is a fluid that is wet.

clue.text: Small state embraced by Italians

parts.note: a tiny independent republic entirely surrounded by Italian territory

explanation.surface: A tiny country hugged by its neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' here means surrounded on every side, not welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny republic is an enclave, a microstate wholly enclosed by Italy.

clue.text: Bound to need back for brief period of extra time

parts.note: a bound is a leap
to back someone is to second or support them

explanation.surface: A jumper needs support during a short spell of extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra time' suggests sport, but it means a second added to clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap second is the single extra second occasionally added to keep clocks in step with the Earth.

clue.text: Hold out with veteran

indicators.note: out indicates the letters are put out of order

parts.note: and joins things, as with does

explanation.surface: Holding out alongside an old soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is an idiom for an experienced person, a veteran.

clue.text: Small amount charged to come to a small island

parts.note: an ion is a tiny particle carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A small charge for taking a boat to a little isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' reads as billed, but it means electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Knocked about, in debt — rate poorly

indicators.note: poorly means done badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battered borrower with a bad credit rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered means beaten or knocked about.

clue.text: Girl who's got married out of spite

indicators.note: out of means the married letter has left the spite word

parts.note: malice is spite

explanation.surface: A girl who married purely out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Alice is a common female first name, as in Lewis Carroll's heroine, so it is one girl.

clue.text: Field where Spanish team fail to appear in second half

indicators.text: fail to appear in second half
indicators.note: the closing part of the club name is missing, leaving only its start and one letter more

parts.note: Real Madrid is the Spanish football club

explanation.surface: A Spanish football side who never turn up after half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team absent after the interval; the parse drops ADRID from REAL MADRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or sphere of activity.

clue.text: Humour Falstaff's drinking partner — it's all the same to Shakespeare

parts.note: wit is humour
Prince Hal is Falstaff's companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: A comic sidekick's attitude to his drinking friend in the plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Withal is an archaic word for nevertheless, common in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Move briskly round a deck

indicators.note: round means the brisk-movement word goes around the other letter

parts.note: to trot is to move briskly

explanation.surface: Jogging around a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' reads as a ship's deck but means a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a deck of cards used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Chirpy little thing languishing with passion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound, not the spelling, is wanted

parts.note: sick means ill or languishing and ardour means passion, together making sick ardour

explanation.surface: A cheerful little creature pining with love.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'sick ardour' matches the insect's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a small insect known for its loud chirping song.

clue.text: Help to put away hi-fi, short of energy for way-out rock

indicators.note: to put away means to enclose, so the help word holds the hi-fi word

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: short of means one letter is missing from the hi-fi word

parts.note: a stereo is a hi-fi system
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Help storing a sound system, low on power, for far-out music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of energy' drops one E from STEREO to give STERO. 'rock' suggests music but means a space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body in space, rock far out in the solar system.

clue.text: At this point, try to listen

indicators.note: to listen signals the word is taken as heard

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: A request to make an effort to listen now.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means in this place or at this point.

clue.text: The way to share, showing restraint

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
a ration is a share

explanation.surface: Sharing as the path to self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation is the avoidance of excess, a synonym of restraint.
